chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji‘abi reported to me, he said: Abul Qasim al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Ja‘far ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, from his father, he said: Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Hashimi narrated to us, he said: Abdul Mu‘min narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them), from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari, who said:

The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: The quickest of things in punishment is a man to whom you do good and he repays your kindness with evil; and a man with whom you made a covenant, and your way is to be faithful to him while his way is to deceive you; and a man against whom you are not insolent, yet he is constantly insolent against you; and a man whose kinship you maintain, yet he cuts you off.

key_terms.إحسان: Goodness, kindness, doing good to others

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the quickest divine punishment?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) identifies four types of social transgressions that attract the swiftest divine punishment: repaying good with evil, breaking covenants despite the other party's faithfulness, persistent aggression against a peaceful person, and severing family ties when the other maintains them. This hadith was taught in the context of establishing ethical norms for interpersonal conduct in the Muslim community, where reciprocity and good faith were foundational principles.
word_analysis: you made a covenant with him

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 5. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji’abi reported to me from Abul Qasim al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Hasan, who reported from Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan, from his father, who reported from Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Hashimi, who reported from Abdul Mu’min, who reported from Muhammad ibn ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon him, that Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari narrated:

The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, said: "The quickest evil consequence is for a man to whom you do a good turn and he pays you back by evil deeds; and a man with whom you have entered into a covenant wishing to fulfil it, while he intends to deceive you; and a person to who you are not insolent, but he persists in his insolence against you; and a person with whom you mend your blood relationship but he cuts you off."
